policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Recitative hoti before direct discourse: ASV 'He that saith, I know him' punctuates the quotation and leaves the conjunction untranslated, so its presence or absence leaves the English identical. No ASV note is mapped here.

ASV 'ought himself also to walk even as he walked' renders kai autos and the comparative kathos; an added correlative houtos is regularly absorbed into 'even as' in English and leaves no separate word, so the rendering does not distinguish the readings.
ASV opens the verse 'Beloved,' which renders Agapetoi; Adelphoi would have produced 'Brethren.' The vocative is a translated word and the ASV wording names it.

ASV ends 'the old commandment is the word which ye heard,' with no closing 'from the beginning.' The phrase ap' arches is rendered earlier in the verse ('which ye had from the beginning'), showing the ASV does translate it where present; its absence after 'ye heard' excludes the longer reading.

ASV 'I have written unto you' twice, with the margin 'Or, I wrote' — both renderings of the aorist egrapsa. The present Grapho would have given 'I write.' The alternative_rendering notes concern English tense wording only and confirm an aorist underlies the text.

ASV 'as ye heard that antichrist cometh' is anarthrous, against 'many antichrists' immediately following; the added article of the alternative reading would have given 'the antichrist,' which the ASV writes nowhere here.

A transposition of ex hemon and esan. English word order in 'if they had been of us' is fixed by its own grammar and cannot reflect the Greek sequence. The mapped note is alternative_rendering and concerns the scope of the negative in the last clause, not this unit.
ASV prints the connective: 'And ye have an anointing from the Holy One, and ye know all things.' The second 'and' renders kai, which the omitting reading lacks.

ASV text reads 'ye know all things' — the accusative object panta. The mapped textual_variant note, 'Some very ancient authorities read and ye all know,' is precisely the nominative pantes and is placed in the margin, so the ASV text chose panta.

ASV prints the clause 'he that confesseth the Son hath the Father also' in the text, which excludes the omission. The remaining two readings are the same words differing only in editorial bracketing, a distinction English cannot register; the ASV carries no italics or note here.

ASV 'As for you, let that abide in you which ye heard from the beginning' renders the emphatic humeis with no inferential particle; the ASV renders oun as 'therefore' where it stands, and none appears.

A transposition of menei and en humin. 'The anointing which ye received of him abideth in you' fixes its order by English grammar. The two mapped notes are alternative_rendering and bear on other clauses of the verse.
ASV 'as his anointing teacheth you' renders the possessive autou; the neuter pronoun auto would have given 'the same anointing' or an unpossessed 'it,' not 'his.'

ASV 'ye abide in him,' with the margin 'Or, abide ye' — indicative and imperative are both readings of the present menete. The future meneite would have required 'ye shall abide,' which neither text nor margin offers.
ASV 'that, if he shall be manifested' renders the conditional ean; hotan would have given 'when he shall be manifested.' The mapped notes are greek_gloss and touch other words in the verse.

Aorist schomen and present echomen of the same verb, both aspectual subjunctives after hina; ASV 'we may have boldness' renders either without distinction. The mapped notes are greek_gloss on 'from him' and 'presence.'
ASV 'ye know that every one also that doeth righteousness is begotten of him' carries 'also,' which renders the added kai; the shorter reading leaves nothing for it to translate.
